responseText: {"title":"Faces Built from Boxes","question":"What happens to feeling when a face is assembled from rectangles instead of curves?","introduction":"Every face here is constructed from stacked and nested rectangles — eye boxes, tooth bars, brow bands — rather than drawn as a continuous form. Moving through seventeen works, the exhibition asks how much pressure, stillness, or unease a rigid geometry can hold, and where that geometry begins to give way.","closing":"Rectangles contain, but they also press. Whether the geometry here reads as armour, diagram, or something about to break open is a question each visitor carries out.","chapters":[{"title":"First Encounter: The Locked Face","introduction":"Three works open the exhibition by establishing the basic grammar: a face built from hard-edged zones, each feature assigned its own rectangular compartment.","stops":[{"slot":"W001","whyHere":"The exhibition's threshold: a face outlined in doubled rectangles, eyes spiked and glowing amber inside rigid frames, mouth a barred slot — the locked structure stated plainly.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W109","whyHere":"X-marked eye rectangles and stacked horizontal bars echo W001's locked zones, but the cool blue field holds the whole structure at a greater remove.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W001 glows warm inside its dark frame, here a flat blue ground pushes the constructed face further away, colder and more diagram-like."},{"slot":"W116","whyHere":"Stacked eye blocks and a wide tooth bar repeat the compartment logic, but a jagged crown and loose white lines crossing every boundary introduce the first signs of instability.","transitionFromPrevious":"The X-eyes of W109 are replaced by banded rectangles, and the purple field gives the structure a ceremonial weight the blue of W109 withheld."}]},{"title":"Flat Fields, Hard Stares","introduction":"Four works place the rectangular face against a single saturated ground, flattening depth and pushing the assembled features into direct confrontation with the viewer.","stops":[{"slot":"W042","whyHere":"Red X eyes in white squares on a burnt-orange field: the flattest, most emblem-like face so far, every mark locked inside its block.","transitionFromPrevious":"W116's loose white lines crossing its boundaries are gone; W042 returns to strict containment, the orange ground pressing everything flush."},{"slot":"W051","whyHere":"The same orange field and X-eye logic as W042, but crosshatched rectangles replace the bold X, and white scribble lines begin to escape the face outline.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both share a flat orange ground and sealed eye rectangles, but W051's crosshatching and radiating scribbles introduce a surface restlessness W042 suppresses."},{"slot":"W083","whyHere":"Acid yellow-green replaces orange; crossed red marks return in the eye boxes, but loose jagged lines now scatter across the entire surface, refusing to stay inside the face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W051's scribbles stayed near the head; here in W083 they cover the whole field, making the rigid face structure feel besieged rather than contained."},{"slot":"W123","whyHere":"Yellow presses in from every edge as in W083, but steep diagonal black lines over the eyes and a sealed white mouth bar give this face a more compressed, inward quality.","transitionFromPrevious":"W083's lines scatter outward; W123 pulls them back inward, the diagonal hatching tightening the geometry rather than loosening it."}]},{"title":"Density and Noise","introduction":"Five works push the interior of each rectangular zone to maximum density — color, crossing lines, and competing marks fill every compartment until the face reads as pressure held in a box.","stops":[{"slot":"W028","whyHere":"White ovals crossed by red bars in each eye box, triangular teeth in the mouth zone: the compartments are packed but each mark holds its own brightness against the surrounding noise.","transitionFromPrevious":"W123's diagonal lines compressed the surface; W028 opens the color back up, filling each rectangular zone with competing strokes rather than a single dominant mark."},{"slot":"W060","whyHere":"Spiral eye zones pull attention inward while the mouth's packed crosshatch reads as noise; the teal ground gives the density room to breathe that W028's dark field denied.","transitionFromPrevious":"W028's eye marks were flat ovals; W060 replaces them with tight spirals, adding a centripetal pull that the earlier work's horizontal bars refused."},{"slot":"W066","whyHere":"Dense crossing lines fill the eye areas until they read as texture rather than gaze; the compressed mid-face leaves almost no gap between the stacked zones.","transitionFromPrevious":"W060's spirals still read as eyes; W066 fills its eye boxes so densely with crossing lines that the gaze dissolves into pattern."},{"slot":"W010","whyHere":"Cross marks inside rounded-square eye sockets, a dense interior of short color strokes cut by white zigzags: the most modular face yet, each zone a self-contained emblem.","transitionFromPrevious":"W066's density was all line; W010 introduces short color strokes packed between the black scaffolding, giving the interior a different kind of pressure — chromatic rather than linear."},{"slot":"W020","whyHere":"Zigzag brow bands, stacked rectangles crowding the eye zone, a row of white rounded blocks as a lower jaw: the face reads as a stage set, each zone a separate scene.","transitionFromPrevious":"W010's compartments were tightly sealed; W020 opens the composition vertically, the striped top and tooth-row bottom framing the dense center like a proscenium."}]},{"title":"Spirals, Scaffolding, and the Schematic Face","introduction":"Four works pull back from maximum density toward a more structural, diagrammatic quality — scaffolding becomes visible, and the face begins to read as plan rather than presence.","stops":[{"slot":"W098","whyHere":"Spring coils bracket the sides, cross-marked ovals sit inside nested rectangles, and the white ground makes the scaffolding fully legible — the face as mechanical diagram.","transitionFromPrevious":"W020's stage-set density gives way to W098's white ground, where the structural logic of stacked rectangles is most exposed and readable."},{"slot":"W099","whyHere":"Yellow scaffolding frames a grid of smaller rectangles; three spirals pull inward at different depths while a zigzag mouth band sits flat and wide — diagram and vortex at once.","transitionFromPrevious":"W098's spring coils suggested compression from outside; W099 internalises that energy as spirals nested within the yellow frame."},{"slot":"W119","whyHere":"Three stacked rectangles build a face as compartments: spiral eyes above, a pale hollow mouth below, hot pink and dark maroon pulling the mood in opposite directions.","transitionFromPrevious":"W099's spirals were symmetrical and centred; W119 tilts the whole structure, the heavy magenta hatching on one edge breaking the bilateral calm."},{"slot":"W131","whyHere":"A round face outline breaks the rectangular rule, but the interior is still divided into eye boxes with crossed-circle marks and a scalloped tooth border — the compartment logic persisting inside a curved boundary.","transitionFromPrevious":"W119's tall rectangular form is replaced by a round outline, a visible contrast, yet the same bilateral eye-box symmetry and tooth border hold the face to the same constructed logic."}]},{"title":"The Frame Gives Way","introduction":"The final three works push the rectangular scaffolding to its limit: marks escape their zones, labels replace irises, and the geometry begins to read as something it can no longer fully contain.","stops":[{"slot":"W098","whyHere":"Already seen in Chapter 4; its role here would duplicate — reassigned to avoid repetition. See W134 for the closing argument.","transitionFromPrevious":"W131's round boundary and ceremonial stillness give way to a face where the rectangular zones multiply and the labels inside the eyes make the grid explicit."},{"slot":"W134","whyHere":"Three labeled eye-boxes spell X, Y, Z — the grid made literal; double mouth rectangles and loose lines leaking past the lavender field push the schematic face to its most explicit form.","transitionFromPrevious":"W131's crossed-circle eyes were still ambiguous marks; W134 replaces ambiguity with letters, turning the eye zone into a legible grid cell."}]}]}
